Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies age 80
stories.summary: Known as the 'Boss of Bosses', he was the head of all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel in the 1980s before his arrest broke up his drug organisation. Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo has died in hospital aged 80. Félix Gallardo was widely considered one of the biggest drug smugglers in history and is credited with building an alliance between criminal groups in Colombia and his own Mexican cartel. Known as The Godfather or the 'Boss of Bosses', Félix Gallardo was the head of the all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel, which reigned over Mexican drug trafficking at the height of the cocaine boom of the 1980s.

more.text: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, who helped build the foundations of modern-day drug empires, was the subject of a major U.S. manhunt for his role in the murder of a D.E.A. agent.

Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in hospital on Sunday aged 80 after suffering multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. Imprisoned since 1989, he had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.

This is where anti-fascists stood up to Oswald Mosley’s Blackshirts, where women established a “ peace camp ” to protest against the rise of nuclear weapons, and where the movement against the poll tax helped to bring down Margaret Thatcher.
